dedupe_keys.name: selsaady1 tsm yield thresholds when does stochastic planning pay off yield uncertainty thresholds for semiconductor supply chain optimization

description: The code author publishes a Python mixed-integer stochastic-planning model for a semiconductor front-end, die-bank and back-end supply chain. Zenodo archives version 1.0 under MIT and links a GitHub repository with the model, experiments, results and CBC solver logs. The README compares a three-stage recourse policy with an expected-value plan under front-end and back-end yield variation. It reports decision thresholds for when stochastic planning improves expected profit and service. This model can support manufacturing-capacity and disruption scenarios. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Coverage is a single-product, single-period stylised chain, not a measured production network. A limitation is that the reported threshold depends on yield distributions, shortage penalties and recourse assumptions. The manuscript is described as submitted, not accepted. The code and solver logs were not executed or independently checked, and the Zenodo abstract itself provides no description beyond the title.
